Natural_Language: Acquisition savings means savings resulting from the application of a value engineering change proposal (VECP) to contracts awarded by the same contracting office or its successor for essentially the same unit. Acquisition savings include instant contract savings, concurrent contract savings, and future contract savings.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_AcqSav_a: Acquisition savings result from VECP application to contracts by same contracting office or successor for same unit; P_48_001_AcqSav_b: Acquisition savings include instant contract savings; P_48_001_AcqSav_c: Acquisition savings include concurrent contract savings; P_48_001_AcqSav_d: Acquisition savings include future contract savings
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating three categories of acquisition savings. All three are included in the definition, making conjunction appropriate.

Natural_Language: Instant contract savings, that are the net cost reductions on the contract under which the VECP is submitted and accepted, and that are equal to the instant unit cost reduction multiplied by the number of instant contract units affected by the VECP, less the contractor's allowable development and implementation costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_AcqSav_1_a: Instant contract savings are net cost reductions on the VECP contract; P_48_001_AcqSav_1_b: Instant contract savings equal instant unit cost reduction times number of affected units minus contractor's allowable development and implementation costs
Validation_Notes: Definitional proposition with two conjunctive elements: what they are and how they are calculated. References contractor's development and implementation costs.

Natural_Language: Concurrent contract savings, that are net reductions in the prices of other contracts that are definitized and ongoing at the time the VECP is accepted.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_AcqSav_2_a: Concurrent contract savings are net price reductions on other contracts; P_48_001_AcqSav_2_b: Those contracts must be definitized and ongoing at VECP acceptance
Validation_Notes: Conditional: savings apply only to contracts definitized and ongoing at VECP acceptance. HIGH-RISK rule used because the temporal condition triggers the savings definition. Implication direction preserved: condition (definitized and ongoing) enables savings.

Natural_Language: Future contract savings, that are the product of the future unit cost reduction multiplied by the number of future contract units in the sharing base. On an instant contract, future contract savings include savings on increases in quantities after VECP acceptance that are due to contract modifications, exercise of options, additional orders, and funding of subsequent year requirements on a multiyear contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_AcqSav_3_a: Future contract savings equal future unit cost reduction times future contract units in sharing base; P_48_001_AcqSav_3_b: On instant contracts, future savings include savings on quantity increases after VECP acceptance from modifications, options, additional orders, and multiyear subsequent year funding
Validation_Notes: Two-part definition: general formula plus conditional elaboration for instant contracts. HIGH-RISK implication used for the instant contract condition. Direction preserved.

Natural_Language: Collateral costs means agency costs of operation, maintenance, logistic support, or Government-furnished property.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_CollCosts_a: Collateral costs are agency costs; P_48_001_CollCosts_b: Categories include operation, maintenance, logistic support, or GFP
Formal_Logic_Statement: P_48_001_CollCosts_a ^ (P_48_001_CollCosts_b1 v P_48_001_CollCosts_b2 v P_48_001_CollCosts_b3 v P_48_001_CollCosts_b4)
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Disjunction appropriate because 'or' is explicitly used -- any one category qualifies as collateral cost.

Natural_Language: Collateral savings means those measurable net reductions resulting from a VECP in the agency's overall projected collateral costs, exclusive of acquisition savings, whether or not the acquisition cost changes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_CollSav_a: Collateral savings are measurable net reductions from VECP in projected collateral costs; P_48_001_CollSav_b: Collateral savings exclude acquisition savings; P_48_001_CollSav_c: Applies whether or not acquisition cost changes
Validation_Notes: Definitional with three conjunctive requirements. Explicit exclusion of acquisition savings and independence from acquisition cost changes. References both acquisition savings and collateral costs definitions.

Natural_Language: Contracting office includes any contracting office that the acquisition is transferred to, such as another branch of the agency or another agency's office that is performing a joint acquisition action.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_ContrOfc_a: Contracting office includes any office the acquisition transfers to; P_48_001_ContrOfc_b: Includes another branch of same agency; P_48_001_ContrOfc_c: Includes another agency's office performing joint acquisition
Validation_Notes: Expansive definition. 'Such as' introduces non-exhaustive disjunctive examples. The parent requirement is that any transferee office counts.

Natural_Language: Contractor's development and implementation costs means those costs the contractor incurs on a VECP specifically in developing, testing, preparing, and submitting the VECP, as well as those costs the contractor incurs to make the contractual changes required by Government acceptance of a VECP.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_DevCosts_a: Costs incurred in developing, testing, preparing, and submitting the VECP; P_48_001_DevCosts_b: Costs incurred to make contractual changes required by Government acceptance of VECP
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Two categories of costs connected by 'as well as' indicating conjunction. Both categories are included in the definition.

Natural_Language: Future unit cost reduction means the instant unit cost reduction adjusted as the contracting officer considers necessary for projected learning or changes in quantity during the sharing period. It is calculated at the time the VECP is accepted and applies either throughout the sharing period or to calculation of a lump-sum payment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_FutUCR_a: Future unit cost reduction is instant UCR adjusted for projected learning or quantity changes; P_48_001_FutUCR_b: CO determines necessary adjustments; P_48_001_FutUCR_c: Calculated at time of VECP acceptance
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating definition with disjunctive application modes. 'Either...or' triggers disjunction for the two application pathways.

Natural_Language: Throughout the sharing period, unless the contracting officer decides that recalculation is necessary because conditions are significantly different from those previously anticipated.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_FutUCR_1_a: Future UCR applies throughout sharing period; P_48_001_FutUCR_1_b: CO may recalculate if conditions significantly differ from anticipated
Validation_Notes: Default application throughout sharing period with exception for CO recalculation. 'Unless' creates negation-triggered conditional. HIGH-RISK implication preserves directionality.

Natural_Language: To the calculation of a lump-sum payment, that cannot later be revised.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_FutUCR_2_a: Future UCR applies to lump-sum payment calculation; P_48_001_FutUCR_2_b: Lump-sum payment cannot later be revised
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive facts: application to lump-sum and prohibition on later revision. Straightforward conjunction.

Natural_Language: Instant contract means the contract under which the VECP is submitted. It does not include increases in quantities after acceptance of the VECP that are due to contract modifications, exercise of options, or additional orders. If the contract is a multiyear contract, the term does not include quantities funded after VECP acceptance. In a fixed-price contract with prospective price redetermination, the term refers to the period for which firm prices have been established.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_InstCont_a: Instant contract is the contract under which VECP is submitted; P_48_001_InstCont_b: Excludes quantity increases after VECP acceptance from modifications, options, or additional orders; P_48_001_InstCont_c: For multiyear contracts, excludes quantities funded after VECP acceptance; P_48_001_InstCont_d: For FP with prospective price redetermination, refers to period with firm prices
Validation_Notes: Complex definitional proposition with general rule plus two contract-type-specific conditionals. HIGH-RISK implications for the conditional clauses ('If the contract is...'). Direction preserved: contract type triggers definitional scope.

Natural_Language: Instant unit cost reduction means the amount of the decrease in unit cost of performance (without deducting any contractor's development or implementation costs) resulting from using the VECP on the instant contract. In service contracts, the instant unit cost reduction is normally equal to the number of hours per line-item task saved by using the VECP on the instant contract, multiplied by the appropriate contract labor rate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_InstUCR_a: Instant UCR is the decrease in unit performance cost from VECP on instant contract; P_48_001_InstUCR_b: Calculation excludes contractor's development or implementation costs; P_48_001_InstUCR_c: For service contracts, equals hours saved per line-item task times contract labor rate
Validation_Notes: Definition with general rule and service-contract-specific conditional. 'Normally equal' in service context introduces advisory element but treated as standard calculation. HIGH-RISK implication for contract-type condition.

Natural_Language: Sharing base means the number of affected end items on contracts of the contracting office accepting the VECP.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_SharingBase_a: Sharing base is the number of affected end items on contracts of the VECP-accepting contracting office
Validation_Notes: Simple definitional proposition. Already atomic. References contracting office definition for scope.

Natural_Language: Sharing period means the period beginning with acceptance of the first unit incorporating the VECP and ending at a calendar date or event determined by the contracting officer for each VECP.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_SharingPeriod_a: Sharing period begins at acceptance of first unit incorporating VECP; P_48_001_SharingPeriod_b: Sharing period ends at CO-determined date or event per VECP
Validation_Notes: Definitional with two conjunctive elements: start condition and end condition. CO discretion on end date noted.

Natural_Language: Unit means the item or task to which the contracting officer and the contractor agree the VECP applies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_Unit_a: Unit is the item or task to which the VECP applies; P_48_001_Unit_b: CO and contractor must agree on what the VECP applies to
Validation_Notes: Definitional requiring bilateral agreement (CO and contractor). Conjunction captures both the definition and the agreement requirement.

Natural_Language: Value engineering proposal means, in connection with an A-E contract, a change proposal developed by employees of the Federal Government or contractor value engineering personnel under contract to an agency to provide value engineering services for the contract or program.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_001_VEProp_a: Value engineering proposal is a change proposal connected to an A-E contract; P_48_001_VEProp_b: Developed by Federal Government employees or contractor VE personnel; P_48_001_VEProp_c: Contractor VE personnel must be under contract to provide VE services
Validation_Notes: Definitional with disjunctive developer categories: government employees OR contractor personnel (with the additional condition that contractor personnel must be under VE services contract).

Natural_Language: Value engineering is a formal technique where contractors may (1) voluntarily suggest more economical methods and share resulting savings or (2) be required to create programs to identify and submit more economical methods to the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_101_a: Value engineering is a formal technique; P_48_101_b: Contractors may voluntarily suggest economical methods and share savings; P_48_101_c: Contractors may be required to create VE programs to identify and submit economical methods
Validation_Notes: General statement establishing VE as a formal technique with two disjunctive modes: voluntary or mandatory. 'May' for the voluntary path, 'be required' for the mandatory path.

Natural_Language: Section 48.102 establishes policies for value engineering including agency VE procedures, non-DoD VE program requirements, and DoD-specific VE program requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_102: Parent aggregating policy subsections
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating three policy subsections. All subsections apply concurrently.

Natural_Language: As 41 U.S.C. 1711 requires, agencies must create and maintain cost-effective value engineering procedures. Agencies must offer contractors substantial financial incentives to develop and submit VECPs. Contracting offices must include value engineering provisions in appropriate supply, service, architect-engineer and construction contracts as sections 48.201 and 48.202 direct, except when the agency head grants exemptions for specific cases or contract classes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_102_a_1: Agencies must create and maintain cost-effective VE procedures per 41 U.S.C. 1711; P_48_102_a_2: Agencies must offer substantial financial incentives for VECPs; P_48_102_a_3: Contracting offices must include VE provisions per 48.201 and 48.202; P_48_102_a_4: Agency head may exempt specific cases or contract classes
Validation_Notes: Multiple mandatory requirements (shall/must) with an exception pathway for agency head exemption. 'Except when' triggers conditional negation. HIGH-RISK implication for the exemption logic. External statutory reference to 41 U.S.C. 1711.

Natural_Language: Non-Department of Defense agencies must use the value engineering program requirement clause (52.248-1, Alternates I or II) in initial production contracts for major systems and for major systems research and development contracts. Exceptions apply when the contracting officer determines and documents that such use is inappropriate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_48_102_b_1: Non-DoD agencies must use 52.248-1 Alt I or II in initial production contracts for major systems; P_48_102_b_2: Must also use in major systems R&D contracts; P_48_102_b_3: CO may determine and document that use is inappropriate (exception)
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate for non-DoD agencies with CO-level exception authority. 'Must' makes requirement mandatory. 'Determines and documents' establishes procedural prerequisite for exception. HIGH-RISK implications for both the trigger condition and exception. Cross-reference to clause 52.248-1.

Atomic_Propositions: P_48_102_c: Parent aggregating DoD VE clause requirement and its exceptions
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate for DoD with disjunctive exceptions. Trigger: DoD + major systems + initial production. HIGH-RISK implication. Cross-reference to DoD Directive 5000.1 (external) and 52.248-1.
